wacc.formula: WACC = wₑ × kₑ + w_d × k_d × (1 − t);  kₑ = r_f + β × ERP

methods.formula: 10-year Monte Carlo: revenue growth switches between high / steady / decline regimes by a Markov chain; margin drifts by regime; value = Σ discounted FCFF − SBC + terminal, per share
assumptions: its own history + the panel prior (markov.json)
methods.fit: It has a DCF and enough quarters of revenue history to estimate how often its growth switches regime.

methods.formula: FCFF = EBIT × (1 − t) + D&A − capex − ΔWC;  EV = Σ FCFF/(1+WACC)^t + TV/(1+WACC)^5;  TV = NOPAT₆ × (1 − g ÷ ROIC) ÷ (WACC − g);  value = (EV − debt + cash − claims) ÷ shares
steps: growth by year 6%, 5%, 4%, 4%, 3%; EBIT margin 11.5%; D&A 3.5% of revenue; capex 3.0% of revenue; ΔWC 10% of each revenue increase
Monte Carlo: 2,000 scenarios, 10th–90th percentile $51.64 – $202.37; P(value > price) = 83%

methods.formula: Graham number = √(22.5 × EPS × book value per share);  22.5 = a P/E of 15 × a P/B of 1.5

assumptions: Benjamin Graham, The Intelligent Investor (1949; 1973 edition, ch. 14)
methods.fit: It has positive earnings and book value, the two things Graham asked a defensive investor to pay for — and to pay little for.

methods.formula: Value = EPS × (8.5 + 2g) × 4.4 ÷ Y;  g = expected yearly growth in percent, Y = the AAA corporate yield today

methods.formula: EPV = adjusted earnings ÷ WACC − net debt;  adjusted earnings = normalized EBIT × (1 − t) + D&A − maintenance capex;  normalized EBIT = average margin × revenue
